paragraphs.text: Reality Fracture is an upcoming Magic: The Gathering expansion, an event set forming the climax of both the Echoverse Arc , the larger three-year Metronome arc, and Jace Beleren 's story. It is scheduled for release on October 2, 2026, and is the 114th Standard expansion set. The set was first teased during the 2023 Announcement Day panel at Gen Con Indiana; the name of the set was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta 2025.

Traumatized by the New Phyrexian Invasion , Jace seeks to remove "suffering" by creating a multiverse without Eldrazi , Nicol Bolas , and Phyrexians known as the Echoverse , which will replace the original. Although other Echoverse planes are briefly visited, the story revolves around an alternate-reality version of the enemy colored Strixhaven : the allied colored Hexhaven. Hexhaven is situated in a geometrically impossible tower whose design has been subconsciously shaped by Jace's experiences. Thus, the set covers three themes: an often requested "What If?" set improving upon Planar Chaos , a dystopian magical school, and an exploration of Jace's character in a mental world .
The main Standard -legal set uses the code FRA. Alternate card frames have a different card number than the original version.
The related non-Standard code is FRC ( Reality Fracture Commander ); these cards are legal in Commander , Legacy , and Vintage , and reprints remain legal where already legal.
Reality Fracture features the return of Special Guests after the releases of Marvel Super Heroes and The Hobbit . The combined art of the cards forms an infinite panorama .

Reality Fracture features 290 regular cards (71 commons, 109 uncommons, 64 rares, 26 mythic rares, 10 basic lands, 10 special) . It becomes available in Play Boosters , Collector Boosters , the Reality Fracture Bundle , a " Secret Lair Bundle ", a Draft Night Box, and one Commander deck , alongside five Foundations Commander Decks .

Each Play Booster features two paired ("echoed") legendary cards (an original character and its Echoverse variant). Although Battlebond had featured a similar gimmick, that only had been possible by printing that set on a one-off specialized printer. For Reality Fracture , another solution was found. The cards were printed side-by-side on the print sheet , and adding three cards from that particular sheet to the booster always includes a complete mirrored pair (and a single card from another mirrored pair). Although there are other Echoverse variants, only the legendary named characters are paired in the packs. To accommodate the density of uncommon legendary creatures, a common slot in the booster and ten common cards in the file were removed, replaced with an uncommon slot and nine uncommon cards. There are 30 borderless echoed pairs cards in the set, i.e., 15 different echoed pairs. Some of the mirrored pairs feature a card that is a reprint, but most of the time both are new cards. Both cards' illustrations are part of the same panorama .
Reality Fracture features one preconstructed Commander deck .
In addition, five "Foundations" Commander decks are being released at the same time, though they are not thematically connected to the main set.

Reality Fracture has a "What if" theme. Unlike Planar Chaos , the set stays true to the color pie ; thus, while Planar Chaos featured colors receiving out-of-color pie mechanics, Reality Fracture features mechanics, factions, and cards brought into a new color with appropriate mechanics and design that stays true to that color.

The marquee mechanic of the set is Empower Jace , which represents the environmentally prevalent antagonism of Jace Beleren . "Empower Jace X" means "put X loyalty counters on a Jace token you control. If you don’t control one, first create a blue Jace planeswalker token with ' −1 : Surveil 1' and ' −3 : Draw a card.'" It is inspired by Amass . As a result, there are multiple cards in the set that synergize with planeswalkers , surveiling, and graveyards.

The set sees the return of preparation cards , which were introduced in Secrets of Strixhaven . To represent the highly regimented curriculum of Hexhaven , however, each school only has a single associated prepare spell which appears on all their preparation cards at uncommon and common :
Fatehold cards have Peer Review , a sorcery with "Create a 2/2 colorless Wizard Soldier creature token named Cadet. Surveil 1."
Theorix cards have Omit Variables , a sorcery with "Mill three cards."
Stingerquill cards have Vicious Verse , a sorcery with "Vicious Verse deals 1 damage to target opponent."
Konstrari cards have Soul Tether , a sorcery with "Create a Heartwood token."
Vigorbloom cards have Seed Suture , a sorcery with "Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature. You gain 1 life."

Each pack contains an Echoed pair, which is a legendary card and an Echoverse version of that card in a different color. Echoverse cards feature a watermark of the Echoverse sigil , as first seen on Ral Zarek, Guest Lecturer ( Secrets of Strixhaven ). With few exceptions, these represent named characters, meaning that most of them are legendary creatures or planeswalkers. As a result, Reality Fracture contains far more planeswalkers than other recent premier sets. However, the set also does have non-creature, non-planeswalker spells that are twists on famous cards.
Domain , proliferate , split second and −1/−1 counters appear as cameo mechanics.

For the first time since War of the Spark , planeswalkers are a major mechanical theme. While that set included a planeswalker card in every pack, the theme is mainly supported in this set by the Jace tokens created by empower Jace, although the set still does have more planeswalkers than average. In fact, there are a few cards that synergize specifically with Jace planeswalkers, including cards that can behold a Jace, which is the first use of the mechanic for types other than creature types .
The set also introduces the predefined Heartwood token (a red and green artifact with " : Add or ") for the Konstrari college.
In Reality Fracture, the limited archetypes of the allied pairs are designed around the colleges of Hexhaven.
: Fatehold Surveil Aggro — Use surveil and foresee the future of your library to build up threats and pressure your opponents.
: Theorix Graveyard Math — Mill yourself to reach threshold and have the graveyard as a source of strength you can count on.
: Stingerquill Face Burn — Add insult to injury by using cards that deal damage directly to your opponent, which in turn lets you strengthen your cards and press the attack.
: Konstrari Mana Ramp — Create Heartwood tokens to get tons of mana and show your opponent the art of building big!
: Vigorbloom Life Gain — Grow your creatures in a variety of ways while boosting life to overwhelm the battlefield with harsh medicine.
Meanwhile, the limited archetypes of the enemy pairs are themed around the Lorwyn Five ( Ajani , Jace , Liliana , Chandra , and Garruk ) and their Echoverse counterparts (or Tamira , in Jace's case).
: Liliana's Attrition — Look to the graveyard for effects that allow you to continue deploying small creatures to the battlefield until you bury your enemies.
: Chandra's Prowess — Cast noncreature spells to trigger abilities and keep up the heat on your opponents.
: Garruk's Bestiary — Bring out fearsome creatures to hunt down your foes. Combine deathtouch and trample to smash through any defenses!
: Ajani's Army — Strengthen your creatures with +1/+1 counters to go aggro with reckless abandon!
: Jace's Mastery — Keep empowering Jace to provide a steady flow of cards or pick your path to victory with cards that grant your planeswalkers abilities!

Overall, the set was designed such that each color has a core theme that acts as a foundation for a Hexhaven pair and " Lorwyn Five " pair. Of note, the color foundational to the pair always appears second in the color pair order.

The previous in-universe set Secrets of Strixhaven continued to build on the years-long story that started all the way back with Jace Beleren in Outlaws of Thunder Junction . Having been traumatized by the suffering of the New Phyrexian Invasion , Jace set about to right what he saw as having gone wrong with the Multiverse . His mysterious plans started with freeing Loot from Maag Taranau . The small, fuzzy creature happens to have a map of all reality in his head, useful for multiverse-spanning plots. That map led Jace to the Meditation Realm in Tarkir: Dragonstorm where Narset and Elspeth witnessed Jace conduct a ritual that went awry, consuming both Jace and the Realm. That led us into Lorwyn Eclipsed , Secrets of Strixhaven , and Reality Fracture . Mastermind Jace has pushed reality to its breaking point. An alternate Multiverse of his own creation threatens to overtake the current one, and just one brave team of heroes stands in the path of oblivion. Jace has created the Echoverse , intended to be free of suffering. While creating the Echoverse, Jace needed a place of abundant magical energy to stabilize it. This inner sanctum is the dystopian school Hexhaven , the Echoverse's version of Strixhaven.

Even though Reality Fracture is setting up a whole new Echoverse, it's not becoming the new norm for Magic going forward. "We are telling a finished story with this set," says Mark Rosewater. "I'm not gonna say that things in this won't matter in the future, but the goal is to make a story and end the story."

A teaser posted to DailyMTG.com in September 2025 included the following line:

In response to early rumors, Head Designer Mark Rosewater had to confirm that same month that the Reality Fracture would not cross Magic 's own lore with that of Universes Beyond . In an interview with TCGPlayer in April 2026, Executive Producer Athena Froehlich hinted that the first-year Strixhaven students introduced in Lorwyn Eclipsed — Abigale , Lluwen , Kirol , Sanar , and Tam —might appear again in Reality Fracture .

In September 2026, the set was announced to take place in an "interesting location" (which would turn out to be the Echoverse ), to have a "cool villain" ( Jace Beleren ), to "build on a theme requested by players for a long time" ("What if" alternate reality), and to "feature an innovative design" (two paired cards in each booster).
The main preview was featured at MagicCon Las Vegas 2026.
The Headliner for this set is Bloodline Recollector , which features a textless retro frame double rainbow foil serialized version (#1–500).

Secret Lair Bundles are a new type of set bundle, featuring promo cards with a full Secret Lair makeover depicting Jace's warped version of the Multiverse. They will be available on October 23, 2026, through the Secret Lair webshop and distributed via WPN stores. Despite being marketed as a Secret Lair product, the cards themselves are part of the Reality Fracture set and use the FRA set code and expansion symbol ( ).

Echoed pairs in the set showcase the original version of a card and its Echoverse counterpart, which have an Echoverse watermark ( ). There are 66 uncommon, 14 rare, and 6 mythic rare individual echoed pairs cards. The 33 uncommon pairs include all 20 permutations of monocolor to monocolor, 2 repeated permutations (noticeably being desparked former planeswalkers and excluding blue), 1 colorless to blue pair (completing color balance), 5 enemy pair to monocolor pairs, and 5 "Way of" enchantment pairs being monocolor to enemy monocolor. The 3 mythic rare pairs include the Lorwyn Five characters that are currently planeswalkers and have Echoverse planeswalker counterparts.

↑ Despite taking the spot of the "Echoverse" card in the pair for Play Booster distribution, Tam, the Possibility and Way of the Paradox do not feature an Echoverse watermark ( ) as both cards refer to Tam , who is a counterpart to Jace Beleren but is not the same character.

Color-shifted cards, which have similar designs to iconic cards from previous sets but in different colors, also appear in this set. However, unlike color-shifted cards in Planar Chaos which violated the mechanical color pie with color bends and breaks , these cards feature larger design changes to best fit the new adopted color. If the card has a "Shattered Mirror" variant, its illustration contains shards that allude to a specific illustration of the referenced card.
Additionally, some prepared spells are color-shifted versions of standalone iconic spells from Magic 's past.

The Heartwood token included in the initial print run of the set used the colorless artifact frame, leaving no indication the token has the colors on the token itself. This issue does not affect gameplay, as the token is just a representation of the game object and will be treated as regardless. A statement in the " Reality Fracture Mechanics" article implies that later print runs of the token will correct this issue.
Gallia, the Merrymaker is missing the word "a" between "with" and "+1/+1 counter" in her second ability.
